docs.focusable.component: `Focusable` is a MARKER, like `Placeable`: presence says "input focus may land here", absence
declines, and no second field can disagree with either answer. It requires `Bounded` — focus
lands on something with a footprint to outline and to hit-test.
import { node, Bounded, Focusable, focusable } from "game-kit"
focusable(field)             // true — the gate the input wiring asks
focusable(node("bar"))       // false — Tab walks past it
## The look and the state are not the atom's
WHICH node holds focus is runtime state the input wiring keeps — never a field on the element,
or two elements would both claim it after one lost message. What focus LOOKS like is a coat the
wiring wears on the focused node — the stock `ring` recipe exists for exactly this — so a
keyboard outline costs no new paint machinery at all.
docs.focusable.focus: Two bars and a Tab key's worth of state. The upper one is `Focusable`; flip `focused` — the
wiring's runtime state — and the story wears a stock ring on it, exactly as a game would on
Tab. The lower bar never rings, whatever the state says: it never declared the capability, and
`focusable()` is the gate the wiring asks before it moves focus at all.
